title: There's No Cat in Catgut
hook: Old violin strings were made from sheep or goat intestines
summary: Despite its name, catgut has never been documented as made from cats. It came mostly from sheep or goat intestines, and some players still use it.

text: The taut strings of a violin.
They used to be made from animal intestines.

panels.mean: Literally "cat gut," a cord made from fibers in animal intestines

text: But it has never been documented as made from cats.
Sheep or goat intestines were what people mostly used.

panels.text: Whoever named it owes the cats an apology

text: Harp, lute, cello and acoustic guitar strings were gut too.
Where the name comes from is unclear.
One theory says "kit," an old word for a small fiddle,
got confused with "kit," a young cat.
Most strings today are steel or synthetic.
Still, classical players keep using gut strings,
because they give a richer, darker sound.

panels.text: So the cats were safe all along
